messages:
laura.eng: Hey team — proposing a per-route "minimal redact" mode for telemetry. Instead of full-text scrub across the board, routes opt into a policy that only keeps non-PII tokens + hashed IDs for dedupe. Goal: keep traceability and prompt-level metrics while reducing utility loss from aggressive redaction.

raj.platform: Can you sketch what 'non-PII tokens' mean in practice? e.g., does it drop emails, names, freeform text?

laura.eng: Short: strip emails, credit-cards, SSNs; mask names (first/last) only if seen as standalone entities; keep adjectives / nouns. We'll keep short span of surrounding context (8 tokens) for quality checks. Also keep a fast-hash for user_id and session_id.

chris-privacy: We need to be careful for GDPR/CCPA. Hashing is ok only if irreversible and salt-per-tenant. Also opt-out must be respected — can we attach consent flags in the routing metadata?

mike-sre: +1 on salt-per-tenant. Operational question: how will this affect sampling and storage size? We can't store full text for all routes.

laura.eng: Proposed flow:
1) Route-level config: redact_mode = [none|minimal|full]
2) If minimal: apply heuristics + fast-hash(user_id, tenant_salt)
3) Sample full-text only for canary tenants (configurable, audit-only) with TTL 7d
4) Inspect mode for support requires an explicit signed breakglass event stored in audit logs

raj.platform: That's reasonable. For canaries — we should ensure feature flag checks at proxy level to avoid routing extra traffic to ingest pipeline. Also need console UI to show when a trace is hashed vs redacted.

deploy-bot: deploy started: feature-flag/per-route-minimal-redact v1 -> staging (job id: 87321)

telemetry-bot: FYI: current ingestion avg event size = 2.1KB, estimated reduction with minimal redact ~35% (back-of-envelope)

chris-privacy: Add to checklist: legal signoff for canary tenants + consent language update. Also confirm HSM keys for tenant salts.

mike-sre: Oncall concern — if a canary triggers a PII leak, we need an immediate scrub flow. Proposal: automatic revocation of canary tokens + background re-scrub job with tombstone markers.

laura.eng: Example config snippet (proto-ish):
```
route_config {
  path: "/v1/generate"
  redact_mode: MINIMAL
  tenant_salt: "use-kms-ref"
  canary_full_text: ["tenant:acme-inc"]
}
```

laura.eng: Example input snippet (before/after):
```
REQ: {"prompt": "Hi I'm Laura, email laura@acme.com, card 4111-1111-1111-1111"}
MINIMAL STORED: {"prompt_tokens": "Hi I'm <NAME>, email <EMAIL>, card <CC_HASH>", "user_hash": "h_7f31..."}
```

raj.platform: How do we measure quality regressions? We need eval sets tied to routes and a dashboard alert if semantic similarity drops >5% after rollout.

laura.eng: Agree. Adding per-route eval sets + a canary window (48h) with automatic rollback if similarity drop >5% or latency regress >20%.

chris-privacy: Make sure support access is logged with session id + legal reason; can't be retroactive unless user consents.

mike-sre: Action items:
- implement tenant-salt KMS integration (mike-sre)
- add proxy flag check + small perf test (raj.platform)
- console indicator + rollout UX (laura.eng)
- legal signoff + consent text (chris-privacy)
- scrub/revoke/playback plan (mike-sre)

laura.eng: OK we'll open RFC and a short-run canary for 3 tenants next week. @chris-privacy can you lead the legal checklist? :pray:

chris-privacy: Yep. I'll prepare a short checklist and pair on the RFC review.

laura.eng: Thanks — will create RFC today and link back here.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: feature-flag/per-route-minimal-redact v1 -> staging (job id: 87321) (0:02)

mike-sre: leaving note: ensure scrub job has idempotent markers `tombstone=true` to avoid double-scrub.

laura.eng: noted. end.
